East is a full side profile: smooth, glossy thorax, banded abdomen with a stinger, and two narrow translucent amber wings folded along the back. North shows the rear: folded wings over a banded abdomen and the stinger pointing at the camera, with only the antenna tips showing above. All three are the same height.

observed.east.png: A side profile of an Earth-style hornet: classic wasp waist, tapered banded abdomen with a stinger, narrow veined amber wings laid flat along the back, head turned right with antennae and mandibles. Smooth, glossy segmented armour. No scales, flame or haze. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: A rear view. The folded wings lie in a symmetric V over a striped abdomen, the stinger tip points toward the camera, legs are splayed and antenna tips show above. No face or eyes. Clean alpha.

observed.flight_1.png: Eight east flight frames. observed.flight_2.png: Eight north flight frames. edits.change: An alien flying insect with a broad, heavy, rounded thorax and a stout tapering abdomen joined to it without a narrow waist, a blunt shielded head, and broad gliding wings; the silhouette is a drifting armoured glider, clearly unlike a hornet.
The head, thorax and abdomen are covered in overlapping heavy scales like shingled armour plates, matte and ash-toned, each scale edged with a clean dark outline.
The scale plating sets the colour: soot-grey and ember-bronze scales in a mottled, scalloped pattern across the whole body, a single uniform palette on every view.
Broad, wide-chord membranous wings with dark veining, folded neatly along the back when grounded and held spread wide in slow, shallow glide strokes in flight.
The flame-proof scale armour is the dominant visual feature of the body on every facing, and the pose is a slow drifting glide rather than an aggressive strike.

Every flight frame uses the same angled game camera as the grounded facings: the north view shows the rear (back, abdomen tip and haunches toward the viewer, eyes hidden), the south view shows the front (face and eyes toward the viewer), the east view shows the right side in profile.
Flight frames show the identical body, scale pattern, palette, proportions and painterly rendering as the grounded facings; only the wing positions differ.
Head, thorax and abdomen keep exactly the same shape, size and position in every flight frame of a facing; only the wings change pose from frame to frame.

Heat is suggested by the body alone: a faint ember-orange glow along the scale edges and in the seams between plates, and the scales themselves clean and untouched; the background is fully transparent.

invariants: transparent background, no flames, haze or scenery baked in
painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline
creature template, flyer module, square sprite canvas for drawSize 2.0 x 2.0
one body plan, one palette (soot-grey and ember-bronze scales) across grounded and flight frames
slow drifting glider character, a lone insect large enough to read as a threat only in swarms
request.prompt: A single alien flying insect, the fire wasp, painted in the vanilla RimWorld sprite style: painterly, realistic, with a clean dark outline, on a fully transparent background. It is a slow, drifting glider that lives in the heat. Its body plan: a blunt shielded head with dark compound eyes, a broad heavy rounded thorax, and a stout tapering abdomen joined to the thorax without a narrow waist, six jointed legs tucked under the body, and short antennae. The head, thorax, abdomen and legs are covered in overlapping heavy scales, like shingled armour plates, matte and ash-toned, each scale edged with a clean dark outline. The scale plating sets the whole colour and pattern: soot-grey and ember-bronze scales in a mottled, scalloped pattern, one uniform palette on every view. Along the scale edges and in the seams between plates there is a faint ember-orange glow, while the scales themselves look clean and untouched by fire. Two pairs of broad, wide-chord membranous wings with dark veining: folded neatly along the back when the insect rests on the ground, and held spread wide in slow, shallow gliding strokes when it flies. Views from the same angled game camera: the east view shows the right side in profile, head toward the right; the north view is a rear view, seen from behind, showing the back, the abdomen tip and the folded or spread wings with the eyes hidden; the south view is a front view, with the face and eyes toward the viewer. Flight frames show exactly the same body, scale pattern, palette, proportions and rendering as the grounded views; the head, thorax and abdomen keep the same shape, size and position in every flight frame, and only the wings change pose. The silhouette reads as an armoured drifting glider, clearly unlike a hornet. Only the insect itself is drawn, centred in the square canvas for a 2.0 by 2.0 draw size, with a transparent background.

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a heavy-bodied snake with bold, even, alternating bands of saturated yellow and black. The underside has a red-orange belly with small yellow-orange fleck patterns. South is a coiled snake with its head raised and facing the camera, and a small pointed spike on top of its head. East is a side profile: a long low coil with the tail trailing left and the head raised on an S-neck on the right. North is a stacked coil, with the neck and head leading away up the image and the tail tip pointing at the viewer. All three have a thick black outline and look clean and glossy.
observed.south.png: A front view of a coiled snake. The head faces the viewer and has two orange eyes with dark slit pupils, a small black spike or horn above the head, and a closed, slightly smiling mouth. No fangs are visible. The throat and belly scales are salmon-red with orange-yellow star-like ember flecks. The coils are bright yellow and black in regular bands, with a fine scale texture. The rim of the belly glows orange-red. It has a heavy black keyline. The background is transparent, with nothing under the body.
observed.east.png: A side profile of the same yellow-and-black banded snake. The body lies in a long flat oval coil, the tail tapers out to the left, and the neck rises in an S-curve to a head facing right with one orange eye. The mouth is closed and no fangs show. There is no head spike. The belly edge is red-orange with ember flecks. There is no ground, ash or roots.
observed.north.png: A rear view. The coil is stacked, the neck rises and recedes away from the viewer, and only the back of the head shows, with no eyes. The tail tip points toward the camera at the bottom centre. The colouring is the same yellow and black bands, with an ember-red belly rim. No head spike is visible. The background is transparent.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom, the snake's coil is about 2.3 cells long beside a vanilla human about 1 cell wide, so it is clearly bigger than the human's footprint. At 32 px per cell the yellow-and-black bands read clearly as a snake and are easily told apart from the brown ground. The rat is much smaller.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the head facing the camera with both eyes, and the throat runs down the front of the coil.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the neck and the back of the head receding away, with no eyes visible and the tail tip toward the camera.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three facings are oblique game-camera views of a coil with visible height. None is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 12%, inside the 15% limit. The panels look comparable.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The palette and banding match across all facings. But the black head spike on south is absent on east (clear profile) and north (back of the head).

SIGNATURE.seen: The defining read is a fire-front ambusher: charred, ember-lit skin and burning-venom fangs. What is drawn is a clean yellow-and-black banded snake, with fire shown only as an orange fleck pattern on the belly. No fangs are visible on any facing.

ALIEN.seen: The regular yellow and black bands read immediately as a banded krait or a yellow-and-black Earth snake. Apart from the belly flecks and a tiny head spike, nothing in the body plan or texture is alien.

DEPARTURES.seen: (1) Charred ash-grey and black scales, cracked like burnt ground: ABSENT. The scales are bright saturated yellow and black in clean bands, uncracked. (2) Ember-orange glow between cracked scales: PARTIAL. Ember flecks appear only on the belly and throat, not between cracks across the back. (3) Oversized fangs glowing ember-hot at the tips: ABSENT. The mouth is closed on south and east. (4) Coiled tight, half-buried in ash and smouldering roots: PARTIAL. STYLE.seen: The flat saturated yellow and black, the uniformly thick black keyline, the glossy round orange eyes and the slight smile all give a toy or sticker look, not painterly vanilla realism.

OURS.seen: It is a bespoke Flamefang-specific design (ember belly, head spike) at the mod's own texPath. It does not match any vanilla or known donor snake.

ALPHA.seen: The cut-out is clean on all three facings: no ground, shadow, ash patch or halo.

SCALE.seen: The description gives no size words. A large coiled snake about 2.3 cells long beside the human is plausible for an ambush serpent.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px per cell the banded coil and raised head read as a snake and stand out strongly from the ground.
